glossary.Orbital tissues: The fat, muscles and connective tissue packed around the eyeball in the orbit.
glossary.Thyroid-associated ophthalmopathy: Another name for thyroid eye disease.
glossary.Ophthalmopathy: Disease of the eye and its surrounding tissues.
glossary.Autoimmune: The immune system attacking the body's own tissue.
glossary.Radioactive iodine ablation: Destroying thyroid tissue with oral radioactive iodine to treat hyperthyroidism.
glossary.Thyrotoxicosis: Excess thyroid hormone in the blood, causing weight loss, tremor and palpitations.
glossary.Type 1 diabetes: Autoimmune loss of pancreatic beta cells causing insulin deficiency.
glossary.Rheumatoid arthritis: Autoimmune inflammatory arthritis of the small joints.
glossary.Gritty eyes: A sandy, foreign-body feeling from a dry ocular surface.
glossary.Cornea: The clear front window of the eye.
glossary.Corneal exposure: Drying of the cornea because the lids do not cover it properly.
glossary.Corneal ulceration: A breach in the corneal surface that can scar and threaten sight.
glossary.Visual acuity: Sharpness of vision, measured with a Snellen chart.
glossary.Colour vision: Ability to tell colours apart; an early loss signals optic nerve damage.
glossary.Optic disc: Where the optic nerve enters the back of the eye, seen with an ophthalmoscope.
glossary.Optic nerve: The nerve carrying visual signals from the eye to the brain.
glossary.Sight-threatening: Likely to cause permanent loss of vision without urgent treatment.
glossary.TFTs: Thyroid function tests: TSH and free T4 (and sometimes T3).
glossary.TSH: Thyroid-stimulating hormone from the pituitary; low in Graves' due to negative feedback.
glossary.T4: Thyroxine, the main hormone made by the thyroid.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging, detailed soft tissue imaging without radiation.
glossary.Lubricating eye drops: Artificial tears that protect a dry or exposed cornea.
glossary.Beta-blocker: A drug such as propranolol that eases tremor and palpitations in thyrotoxicosis.
glossary.Definitive thyroid treatment: Permanent treatment of Graves': radioactive iodine or thyroidectomy.
glossary.IV corticosteroids: Steroids by drip, such as methylprednisolone, to damp orbital inflammation.
glossary.Fibroblast: A connective tissue cell that makes matrix and scar tissue.
glossary.Antigen: A molecule recognised by the immune system.
glossary.TSH receptor: The receptor on thyroid cells that TSH binds; also on orbital fibroblasts.
glossary.Thyroid follicular cells: The thyroid cells that make thyroid hormone, targeted in Graves'.
glossary.Autoantibodies: Antibodies directed against the body's own proteins.
glossary.IGF-1 receptor: Insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor, which may also be stimulated in thyroid eye disease.
glossary.Orbital fat: Fat behind the eyeball that expands in thyroid eye disease.
glossary.Bony orbit: The rigid bone socket containing the eye, which cannot expand.
glossary.Cytokines: Signalling proteins released by immune cells that drive inflammation.
glossary.Oxidative stress: Damage from reactive oxygen molecules outweighing the body's defences.
glossary.EOMs: Extraocular muscles, the six muscles that move each eye.
glossary.GAGs: Glycosaminoglycans, water-attracting sugar chains that cause tissue swelling.
